questions.question: Summarize the presentations on working design, technical functions, functional requirements.
questions.reference_answer: Firstly, Industrial Designer presented on working design, identifying a few basic components of the remote. From the functional design perspective, Industrial Designer introduced what exactly the components were and how they worked with each other. Next, User Interface presented on technical functions design and personally suggested a small size of remote, red in colour and easy to use with must-have buttons. Then, Marketing presented on functional requirements and suggested the group aiming at both the functionality and beauty of the remote.

oracle.answer:
The Industrial Designer presented on the working design and technical functions of the remote control. They identified the basic components and how they interact, including the energy source feeding into the chip and user interface. The remote control's functions were simplified to focus solely on television operations, removing outdated features like teletext. The design should be unique, incorporating color and the company's slogan. The core functionality involves the chip processing user inputs from the interface and generating an infrared signal to the TV. Future upgrades should keep the design simple and technologically current.

The User Interface discussed the technical functions, emphasizing the primary role of the remote control in sending signals to the TV for actions such as turning it on/off, changing channels, and adjusting volume. They suggested keeping the design minimalistic, focusing on essential buttons and avoiding unnecessary complexity. The inclusion of additional functionalities like DVD operation was ruled out due to recent updates.

Marketing provided insights based on a survey, indicating that users prefer a remote control that looks good and matches their behavior. Users frequently use channel selection and volume adjustment buttons, while other buttons are rarely used. The remote should be intuitive, ergonomic, and potentially include features like voice recognition and a locator. The design should be sleek, stylish, and functional, with a long battery life and possibly solar-powered.

questions.question: Why did Project Manager think of the advanced technology design when presenting the technical functions?
questions.reference_answer: Industrial Designer suggested the group could keep the design as simple and clear as possible because this would help them to upgrade their technology at a future point of time. Project Manager asked about the cost at this point, however, Industrial Designer had no idea about what each component cost. So Project Manager thought it should be considered because the price would increase if they were using more advanced technology.

oracle.answer: The evidence provided does not contain any statement from the Project Manager about thinking of advanced technology design when presenting the technical functions. The Project Manager's comments were mainly about cost considerations related to using advanced technology, but there is no explicit mention of them thinking about advanced technology design during a presentation of technical functions. Therefore, based on the given excerpts, the evidence is insufficient to answer the question.

questions.question: Why did the group think of the locator when presenting the functional requirements?
questions.reference_answer: When Marketing mentioned about the long battery life, the group came up with the locator that the remote could beep when users clapped. Also, this function should be designed to not beep every five minutes so that users would not like the remote. The group mates agreed on it and thought it was an interesting and excellent idea.

oracle.answer: The group thought of the locator when presenting the functional requirements because they wanted a feature similar to those found in mobile phones or key finders, which helps locate the remote control easily. This idea came up as part of discussing additional useful features beyond a long battery life, with suggestions including a unique sound activation method (like clapping) to avoid frequent beeping that might annoy users.

questions.question: Summarize the group discussion about general requirements.
questions.reference_answer: The group had a discussion about the target age group and they agreed to look at 15 to 35 year olds. Also, they decided to make it look simple, but still have those key buttons so it would be easy to use. Lastly, the group agreed to include one sort of menu button and voice recognition as an option.

oracle.answer:
The group discussed targeting a broad age range of young people, specifically from fifteen to thirty-five years old, for their new remote control product. They agreed that this demographic values stylish design and is more likely to afford a premium product due to higher disposable income. Voice recognition was identified as a key feature, though its implementation details and feasibility were questioned. The team decided to include voice recognition as an optional feature alongside traditional buttons, emphasizing simplicity and ease of use. They also considered adding a beeper function to help locate the remote control. The general requirements summarized include:

- Targeting the age group of fifteen to thirty-five years old.
- Stylish and sleek design.
- Key buttons for essential functions.
- Optional voice recognition feature.
- Beeper function for locating the remote control.
- Ensuring the product remains affordable and user-friendly.

questions.question: What did the group think of disposable income when discussing general requirements?
questions.reference_answer: Industrial Designer suggested they should also look up popularity among the 25 to 35 years old age group if they looked into a stylish design. Marketing said it was 70% popular among this age group and thought this age group didn't have much economic burden so the remote price should not be unaffordable. User Interface supplemented that their remote might not function with the old TV. Therefore, the group decided to include both 15 to 25 and 25 to 35 years old age group into consideration.

oracle.answer: The group discussed disposable income in relation to targeting different age groups for their product. They noted that people aged twenty-five to thirty-five had a high popularity rate (76.3%) for their product. When discussing the fifteen to twenty-five-year-old age group, Marketing highlighted that this group has a higher disposable income because they typically do not have significant financial commitments such as mortgages, life insurance policies, or cars. Project Manager agreed, adding that this age group has fewer commitments. They concluded that the product price of twenty-five Euros was affordable for young people. However, User Interface raised concerns about whether people in this age group actually needed the product and whether their TVs would be compatible with the new remote control. Despite these concerns, Marketing emphasized that the high interest rate (ninety-one point two percent) among fifteen to twenty-five-year-olds and their disposable income made them a valuable target market. The group ultimately agreed that both age groups could be targeted since they are still relatively young.

questions.question: Why did Project Manager think that they should try to incorporate voice recognition when discussing general requirements?
questions.reference_answer: Project Manager thought since they not only targeted 15 to 35 years old age groups, they should have an implementation for voice recognition technology. Industrial Designer mentioned that voice recognition was not yet a mature technology and most remotes went for buttons to change channels. User Interface suggested they need to have both features and group mates agreed on it.

oracle.answer: Project Manager suggested incorporating voice recognition when discussing general requirements because it aligns with sophisticated features and could potentially enhance user interaction with the TV remote. However, Project Manager also acknowledged the limitations and uncertainties regarding its implementation and effectiveness, as indicated by the discussion on technical specifications and the feasibility of voice commands in a TV remote context.
